newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan low rate policy mustn't be changed-Keidanren.
newsitem.headline: Japan low rate policy mustn't be changed-Keidanren.

text.p: Japan may have to keep its low interest rate policy unchanged to support the economy, Shoichiro Toyoda, chairman of the Federation of Economic Organisations (Keidanren), said on Monday.
In a joint news conference with the heads of three other business groups, Toyoda said the Japanese economy is not making a full-fledged recovery yet.
"The current interest rate policy may have to be kept unchanged to support the economy," he said.

Echoing that view on interest rate policy, Jiro Nemoto, chairman of Japan's Federation of Employers' Associations, said the government must take other steps to help people dependent on interest-rate payments.
The four leaders agreed that the economy will grow steadily in 1997/98 only if various reforms, including administrative and fiscal reforms, actually take place.
Kosaku Inaba, chairman of the Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry, said: "The problem is that people are uneasy about the future of the economy."
Toyoda said the economy was likely to improve in the January-March period due to stepped-up purchases ahead of a planned increase in the consumption tax.
"After April, we are going to have a very difficult situation. The economy depends on how positively the government carries out fiscal reforms, deregulation and other reforms," Toyoda said.
